params.content_kind: flagship corpus (frozen before results): conventional baseline

limitations: this is the flagship B0/B1 CONVENTIONAL-BASELINE result, not yet the B1-vs-VOLE comparison: the `u1_literal_bytes` row is the canonical universal fallback representation, NOT the inverse compiler's selected VOLE representation for the object. The selected-representation comparison needs an exact full-object inverse container (the Phase-K compiler is bounded to 65,536 frames) and is a later increment

B1 is a comparator with zero VOLE semantic authority: it never decides anything about a SampleObject, and its only correctness requirement is an exact round trip of the same canonical i32 information the VOLE representation carries

this is a size/exactness comparison at the object level, not a real-time or playback comparison; B2–B4 (sampler/disk/compressed-file playback) are NOT_IMPLEMENTED in this increment and remain visible in the ladder manifest

the `reference_flac` row is NON-AUTHORITATIVE and outside the frozen result vector: it runs the system `flac` at the same settings when installed, and is NOT_AVAILABLE otherwise. B1 itself never depends on it. It exists because the ported encoder is libFLAC 1.4.3, which does not select the CONSTANT subframe at >=28 bits/sample (an all-zero 32-bit block costs about one bit per sample), while newer reference encoders do; recording both is what stops that divergence from silently flattering the comparison

the five objects above FLAC's 8-channel ceiling appear explicitly as NOT_APPLICABLE_BY_FORMAT_DOMAIN (in `unsupported_objects`) and their bytes never enter a B1 aggregate; `b1_comparable` is derived from the channel count, not read from the manifest
the result is bound to the frozen population: the static projection covers the manifest and corpus hashes, the object order, and each object's canonical i32 hash, rate, channels, frames and byte rows

b1_implementation.description: pure-Rust, forbid(unsafe_code), byte-exact port of libFLAC 1.4.3
b1_implementation.conversion: none (exact canonical interleaved i32; no shift, dither, normalisation or resampling)
b1_implementation.library_baseline_semantics: libFLAC 1.4.3: at >=28 bits/sample the CONSTANT subframe is not selected, so a zeroed block costs about one bit per sample; the non-authoritative `reference_flac` row records where a newer reference encoder differs
b1_implementation.primary_choice: level 5 is the official flac tool's default and libFLAC's documented default, so it is the conventional target

ladder.where: D2 is future conceptual; the row stays visible
